builds.name: Reference: Ranked jungle core
builds.goal: Reference for Fiddlesticks: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ jungle players use most (1,199 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 49.2% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: An ambush mage who uses vision denial and fear to create time for channels. Completing W and keeping enemies in Crowstorm matter more than ordinary attack output. The current jungle provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Hextech Rocketbelt → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass. Electrocute keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Sorcerer's Shoes, Rabadon's Deathcap, Void Staff.
builds.summary: The proven jungle baseline: Hextech Rocketbelt → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass, with Electrocute.
testPlan: Play it in jungle as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Hextech Rocketbelt → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 49.2% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Hextech Rocketbelt → Shadowflame → Zhonya's Hourglass.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula: Fiddlesticks' trinket is replaced by Scarecrow Effigies. When discovered by enemies, Effigies briefly impersonate Fiddlesticks. If Fiddlesticks does not move for 2 seconds, he will impersonate an Effigy. At level six Effigies reveal nearby wards for 6 seconds.

Fiddlesticks channels and drains the souls of nearby enemies, dealing [60 / 90 / 120 / 150 / 180 + (0.45) × AP] magic damage per second for 2 seconds, plus [12 / 14.5 / 17 / 19.5 / 22]% missing Health magic damage at the end. Fiddlesticks restores [25 / 32.5 / 40 / 47.5 / 55]% of damage as Health.

If Fiddlesticks ends the channel without interruption, the remaining Cooldown is reduced by 60%.

Passive: While unseen and out of combat or impersonating an Effigy, damaging an enemy with an ability Fears them for [1.2 / 1.4 / 1.6 / 1.8 / 2] second(s).

Active: Fear an enemy for [1.2 / 1.4 / 1.6 / 1.8 / 2] second(s) and deal [0.04 / 0.045 / 0.05 / 0.055 / 0.06 + (0.0003) × AP] current Health magic damage. If the target has recently been Feared by Fiddlesticks, instead deal [(0.04 / 0.045 / 0.05 / 0.055 / 0.06 + (0.0003) × AP) × (2)] current Health magic damage.
Fiddlesticks channels for [1.5] seconds, then teleports and unleashes a murder of crows, dealing [(150 / 250 / 350 + (0.5) × AP) × (5)] magic damage over [5] seconds.

Fiddlesticks unleashes dark magic, dealing [70 / 105 / 140 / 175 / 210 + (0.5) × AP] magic damage and Slowing by [(-0.3 / -0.35 / -0.4 / -0.45 / -0.5) × -100]% for [1.25] seconds. Enemies in the center are also Silenced for the duration.

builds.name: Unbroken harvest frontliner
builds.summary: Test unbroken harvest frontliner against the conventional damage pattern at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test unbroken harvest frontliner against the conventional damage pattern at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Bountiful Harvest heals for damage dealt and refunds 60% remaining cooldown only when its two-second channel finishes. Aftershock from fear buys a short resistance window; Visage and Riftmaker support draining while Liandry supplies magic pressure.
testPlan: Required state: Fear or silence available to protect the entire channel.
Compare complete and interrupted channels, recording healing and next-W timing.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: A single interruption loses final missing-health damage and the refund.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Durability does not make the channel unstoppable.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Riftmaker, Liandry's Torment, Abyssal Mask, Spirit Visage, Void Staff, Mercury's Treads. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Survive the engage
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Fiddlesticks: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: An ambush mage who uses vision denial and fear to create time for channels. Completing W and keeping enemies in Crowstorm matter more than ordinary attack output. Measure uninterrupted W channels and enemies staying inside Crowstorm. Fear depends on actual vision state; spell damage cannot assume an unseen five-person ambush every time. A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
builds.summary: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts.
testPlan: Kit question for Fiddlesticks: Measure uninterrupted W channels and enemies staying inside Crowstorm. Fear depends on actual vision state; spell damage cannot assume an unseen five-person ambush every time.

Start with the early core (Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: A transformed mana shield, stasis and a spell shield may preserve repeat casts. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Fiddlesticks damaging enemies with spells while unseen or targeting an enemy with Terrify's activation strikes a target unit with fear, causing it to flee in terror for a duration. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.

The route fails Fiddlesticks's stated kit question: Measure uninterrupted W channels and enemies staying inside Crowstorm. Fear depends on actual vision state; spell damage cannot assume an unseen five-person ambush every time.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Defensive redundancy can sacrifice too much damage; this is conditional on real threats.
Full cost 16,000 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Archangel, then the defense matching the opponent. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Banshee's Veil, Rylai's Crystal Scepter, Void Staff are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.
